name: Methane
fact: Simplest alkane; major component of natural gas; used in JEE as the base case for sp3 hybridization.

name: Ethane
fact: Two-carbon alkane; formed by coupling of two methyl radicals; illustrates free rotation about C-C single bond.

name: Propane
fact: Three-carbon alkane stored as LPG; important JEE topic for isomer counting starting from C4.

name: Butane
fact: First alkane with a structural isomer (isobutane); used in JEE to introduce constitutional isomerism.

name: Pentane
fact: Five-carbon alkane with three structural isomers; important for practising IUPAC nomenclature in JEE.

name: Hexane
fact: Common non-polar solvent with five structural isomers; used in JEE problems on liquid-liquid extraction.

name: Heptane
fact: Seven-carbon alkane; octane rating reference (heptane = 0 octane) tested in JEE fuel-chemistry questions.

name: Octane
fact: Eight-carbon alkane; iso-octane defines octane-100 rating; used in JEE combustion enthalpy calculations.

name: Isobutane
fact: Branched isomer of butane (2-methylpropane); classic JEE example of a structural isomer with a tertiary carbon.

name: Neopentane
fact: 2,2-dimethylpropane; has only primary C-H bonds and a single quaternary carbon; important JEE isomer example.

name: Ethene
fact: Simplest alkene with sp2 carbons; plant hormone that ripens fruit; central to JEE electrophilic addition reactions.

name: Propene
fact: Three-carbon alkene; Markovnikov addition of HBr gives 2-bromopropane; key JEE regiochemistry example.

name: 1-Butene
fact: Terminal alkene; undergoes Wacker oxidation to butanone; JEE tests its comparison with 2-butene stability.

name: Isobutylene
fact: 2-Methylpropene; a highly substituted alkene more stable than 1-butene; JEE Zaitsev rule example.

name: 1,3-Butadiene
fact: Conjugated diene; monomer of synthetic rubber; JEE Diels-Alder reactions require understanding its s-cis conformation.

name: Isoprene
fact: 2-Methylbuta-1,3-diene; building block of natural rubber and terpenes; tested in JEE polymer and natural product chapters.

name: Ethyne
fact: Simplest alkyne with sp carbons; acidic terminal H reacts with Na to give sodium acetylide; classic JEE acidity comparison.

name: Propyne
fact: Three-carbon terminal alkyne; reacts with AgNO3 to form silver acetylide precipitate; standard JEE qualitative test.

name: 1-Butyne
fact: Terminal alkyne isomeric with 1,3-butadiene; JEE tests distinguishing terminal vs internal alkynes by reaction with Tollens.

name: Cyclopropane
fact: Three-membered ring with 60 degree bond angles causing angle strain; undergoes ring-opening addition like alkenes in JEE.

name: Cyclobutane
fact: Four-membered ring; more stable than cyclopropane but still strained; JEE angle-strain and torsional-strain comparisons.

name: Cyclopentane
fact: Five-membered ring; nearly strain-free and adopts an envelope conformation; common scaffold in JEE steroid problems.

name: Cyclohexane
fact: Six-membered ring; chair conformation is strain-free; equatorial vs axial preference is a standard JEE conformational analysis topic.

name: Chloromethane
fact: Methyl chloride; simplest haloalkane; undergoes SN2 with no competing E2; textbook JEE nucleophilic substitution example.

name: Dichloromethane
fact: Common polar aprotic solvent used in extractions; JEE reaction medium for many electrophilic reactions.

name: Chloroform
fact: Trichloromethane; used in JEE Reimer-Tiemann reaction to make salicylaldehyde from phenol.

name: Carbon Tetrachloride
fact: Tetrachloromethane; non-polar solvent; JEE uses it as a classic example of a molecule with zero dipole moment despite polar bonds.

name: Bromomethane
fact: Methyl bromide; better leaving group than chloride; JEE SN2 reactivity order: RI > RBr > RCl > RF.

name: Iodomethane
fact: Methyl iodide; most reactive methyl halide toward SN2; used in JEE Menshutkin reaction examples.

name: Chloroethane
fact: Ethyl chloride; undergoes E2 elimination to give ethene with strong base; JEE competition between SN2 and E2.

name: Bromoethane
fact: Ethyl bromide; reacts with Mg in dry ether to form Grignard reagent; cornerstone of JEE organometallic chemistry.

name: Vinyl Chloride
fact: Chloroethene; monomer of PVC; the C-Cl bond is strengthened by resonance with the double bond, making it less reactive in SN reactions.

name: Methanol
fact: Simplest alcohol; toxic to humans; oxidised by KMnO4 to give formaldehyde then formic acid in JEE oxidation sequences.

name: Ethanol
fact: Common alcohol produced by fermentation; gives iodoform (yellow ppt) with I2/NaOH — classic JEE methyl ketone test.

name: Propan-1-ol
fact: Primary alcohol; oxidised to propanal and then propanoic acid; JEE Lucas test gives turbidity slowly (primary alcohol).

name: Propan-2-ol
fact: Secondary alcohol (isopropanol); Lucas test gives immediate turbidity; oxidised to acetone used in JEE iodoform test.

name: Butan-1-ol
fact: Four-carbon primary alcohol; JEE dehydration with H2SO4/443K gives 1-butene (major) illustrating Zaitsev rule.

name: Ethylene Glycol
fact: 1,2-Ethanediol; antifreeze agent; JEE uses it to illustrate how vicinal diols are cleaved by periodic acid.

name: Glycerol
fact: 1,2,3-Propanetriol; byproduct of soap making (saponification); tested in JEE esterification and hydrolysis problems.

name: Tert-Butanol
fact: Tertiary alcohol; Lucas test gives immediate turbidity; dehydration gives isobutylene; JEE SN1 vs SN2 comparison.

name: Phenol
fact: Simplest phenol; more acidic than alcohols due to resonance stabilization of phenoxide; JEE comparing pKa of phenol vs alcohols.

name: Catechol
fact: 1,2-Dihydroxybenzene (o-dihydroxybenzene); readily oxidised; tested in JEE as an ortho isomer in phenol disubstitution.

name: p-Cresol
fact: 4-Methylphenol; methyl group activates ring toward electrophilic substitution; JEE directer effects on substituted phenols.

name: Dimethyl Ether
fact: Methoxymetane; structural isomer of ethanol; lower boiling point than ethanol since it cannot hydrogen bond with itself.

name: Diethyl Ether
fact: Classic extraction solvent; cleaved by HI to give ethyl iodide and ethanol; JEE ether cleavage mechanism.

name: Anisole
fact: Methoxybenzene; methoxy group is ortho/para director; JEE electrophilic aromatic substitution on activated ring.

name: Tetrahydrofuran
fact: Cyclic ether widely used as aprotic solvent for Grignard reactions; JEE distinguishes it from open-chain ethers.

name: Methanal
fact: Formaldehyde; simplest aldehyde with no alpha-H undergoes Cannizzaro reaction; JEE distinguishing Cannizzaro vs aldol.

name: Ethanal
fact: Acetaldehyde; gives iodoform with I2/NaOH; undergoes aldol condensation; JEE nucleophilic addition mechanism.

name: Propanal
fact: Three-carbon aldehyde; Tollens test gives silver mirror; JEE comparison of oxidation states between alcohols and aldehydes.

name: Butanal
fact: Butyraldehyde; aldol condensation gives 2-ethyl-2-butenal; JEE mechanism of base-catalysed aldol condensation.

name: Benzaldehyde
fact: Aromatic aldehyde with no alpha-H; undergoes Cannizzaro and benzoin condensation; JEE classic named reactions.

name: Propanone
fact: Acetone; simplest ketone; gives iodoform test positive; important JEE solvent and reagent in nucleophilic addition.

name: Butanone
fact: Methyl ethyl ketone; JEE tests which alpha-C (more or less substituted) is preferentially halogenated under acid vs base.

name: Acetophenone
fact: Methyl phenyl ketone; gives positive iodoform test; JEE Clemmensen reduction converts it to ethylbenzene.

name: Cyclohexanone
fact: Cyclic ketone; starting material for caprolactam (nylon-6); JEE Beckmann rearrangement produces caprolactam.

name: Formic Acid
fact: Methanoic acid; strongest simple carboxylic acid; reduces Tollens and Fehling reagents (has aldehyde-like H); JEE anomaly.

name: Acetic Acid
fact: Ethanoic acid; forms dimers via H-bonding; reacts with PCl5 to give acetyl chloride; JEE nucleophilic acyl substitution.

name: Propanoic Acid
fact: Three-carbon carboxylic acid; Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction bromination at alpha-C; JEE functional group interconversion.

name: Butanoic Acid
fact: Butyric acid; found in rancid butter; JEE decarboxylation on heating with soda lime gives propane.

name: Benzoic Acid
fact: Aromatic carboxylic acid; decarboxylates on heating with soda lime to give benzene; JEE named reaction: Kolbe synthesis.

name: Oxalic Acid
fact: Ethanedioic acid; reduces KMnO4 (used in JEE titrations); forms insoluble calcium oxalate precipitate as a qualitative test.

name: Lactic Acid
fact: 2-Hydroxypropanoic acid; has one chiral centre; classic JEE optical isomerism example with enantiomers.

name: Citric Acid
fact: Tricarboxylic acid found in citrus fruits; meso-form; JEE uses it for counting acidic H and esterification equivalents.

name: Methyl Acetate
fact: Simplest acetate ester; saponification with NaOH gives sodium acetate and methanol; JEE Fischer esterification mechanism.

name: Ethyl Acetate
fact: Common ester solvent with fruity smell; Claisen condensation with two molecules gives ethyl acetoacetate; JEE condensation reactions.

name: Ethyl Formate
fact: Formate ester with rum-like aroma; hydrolysis gives formic acid and ethanol; JEE isomers of C3H6O2 include this, methyl acetate, and propanoic acid.

name: Acetyl Chloride
fact: Most reactive acyl chloride; reacts vigorously with water and alcohols; JEE acylation of amines and Friedel-Crafts acylation.

name: Acetic Anhydride
fact: Anhydride of acetic acid; acetylates aniline to acetanilide; JEE step in aspirin synthesis and amine protection.

name: Acetamide
fact: Simplest amide; Hofmann bromamide reaction converts it to methylamine; JEE amide hydrolysis and Hofmann degradation.

name: Methylamine
fact: Primary aliphatic amine; more basic than ammonia due to +I effect of methyl; JEE basicity order of amines.

name: Dimethylamine
fact: Secondary amine; most basic among methylamines in aqueous solution; JEE Hinsberg test distinguishes primary, secondary, tertiary amines.

name: Trimethylamine
fact: Tertiary amine; least basic of the trimethyl series in water due to solvation effects; JEE aqueous vs gas-phase basicity discussion.

name: Ethylamine
fact: Primary amine; reacts with HNO2 to give unstable diazonium ion that decomposes to alcohol; JEE diazotization of aliphatic amines.

name: Aniline
fact: Primary aromatic amine; less basic than aliphatic amines; diazotization at 0-5 C gives benzenediazonium used in JEE coupling reactions.

name: Acetonitrile
fact: Methyl cyanide; polar aprotic solvent; hydrolysis gives acetic acid; JEE conversion of halide to nitrile then acid.

name: Nitromethane
fact: Simplest nitro compound; reduced by Fe/HCl or H2/Pd to give methylamine; JEE reduction of nitro compounds.

name: Urea
fact: Diamide of carbonic acid; first organic compound synthesized from inorganic material (Wohler, 1828); pivotal in JEE organic chemistry history.

name: Benzene
fact: Archetypal aromatic compound; Huckel rule (6 pi electrons); undergoes EAS not addition; central to JEE aromatic chemistry.

name: Toluene
fact: Methylbenzene; methyl group activates ring and directs ortho/para; side-chain oxidation with KMnO4 gives benzoic acid in JEE.

name: o-Xylene
fact: 1,2-Dimethylbenzene; oxidised by KMnO4 to phthalic acid; JEE isomers of xylene and their oxidation products.

name: Styrene
fact: Vinylbenzene; monomer of polystyrene; JEE tests reactivity of its conjugated vinyl group toward electrophilic addition.

name: Naphthalene
fact: Bicyclic aromatic (10 pi electrons); EAS favours C1 position; JEE uses it to illustrate fused aromatic ring reactivity.

name: Chlorobenzene
fact: Haloarene; Cl deactivates the ring but directs ortho/para; C-Cl bond strengthened by resonance, resists SN2 — classic JEE inductive vs resonance effect.

name: Nitrobenzene
fact: Nitro group strongly deactivates ring and directs meta; reduction with Fe/HCl gives aniline; central to JEE amine synthesis.

name: Bromobenzene
fact: Aryl bromide; reacts with Mg to give phenylmagnesium bromide (Grignard); JEE aromatic Grignard and cross-coupling reactions.

name: Glycine
fact: Simplest amino acid; no chiral centre; zwitterion at isoelectric point; JEE amino acid structure and isoelectric pH calculations.

name: Alanine
fact: Simplest chiral amino acid (L-form in proteins); JEE optical isomerism and peptide bond formation using alanine as example.

name: Glucose
fact: Aldohexose with 4 chiral centres (16 stereoisomers); open-chain form reduces Tollens/Fehling; JEE carbohydrate chemistry.

name: Fructose
fact: Ketohexose isomer of glucose; reduces Fehling (via enolization); JEE tests why ketosugars are reducing sugars.

name: Sucrose
fact: Disaccharide of glucose and fructose linked by alpha-1,beta-2 glycosidic bond; non-reducing sugar; JEE hydrolysis gives invert sugar.

name: Aspirin
fact: Acetylsalicylic acid; synthesised by acetylation of salicylic acid with acetic anhydride; classic JEE esterification example.

name: Paracetamol
fact: 4-Acetamidophenol (N-acetyl-p-aminophenol); amide bond formed by acetylation of amine; JEE functional group identification.

name: Ibuprofen
fact: Propionic acid NSAID with one chiral centre; sold as racemate; JEE optical activity and resolution of enantiomers.

name: Caffeine
fact: Purine alkaloid (1,3,7-trimethylxanthine); stimulant in coffee and tea; JEE alkaloid structural recognition question.

name: Vanillin
fact: 4-Hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde; flavouring in vanilla; JEE functional group identification (aldehyde + phenol + ether in one molecule).

name: Acrylonitrile
fact: Vinyl cyanide; monomer of polyacrylonitrile (Orlon); JEE addition polymerization and synthetic fibre chapter.

name: Tetrafluoroethylene
fact: Monomer of PTFE (Teflon); extreme thermal and chemical stability due to strong C-F bonds; JEE fluoropolymer addition polymerization.

name: Methyl Methacrylate
fact: Monomer of PMMA (Plexiglas/Perspex); transparent thermoplastic; JEE polymer classification and uses.

name: Caprolactam
fact: Cyclic amide (lactam); monomer of Nylon-6 by ring-opening polymerization; JEE distinguishes Nylon-6 (addition) from Nylon-6,6 (condensation).

name: Nonane
fact: 9-carbon straight-chain alkane found in kerosene and refined petroleum fractions.

name: Decane
fact: 10-carbon straight-chain alkane used as standard reference for fuel droplet evaporation.

name: Isooctane
fact: 2,2,4-Trimethylpentane; defines the 100-point standard for octane rating in gasoline.

name: Isopentane
fact: 2-Methylbutane; branched isomer of pentane with low boiling point (28°C), used in geothermal power cycles.

name: 2,3-Dimethylbutane
fact: Formed via Wurtz reaction of 2-chloropropane with metallic sodium in dry ether.

name: 3-Methylpentane
fact: Constitutional isomer of hexane featuring a symmetrical tertiary carbon.

name: 2,2-Dimethylbutane
fact: Neohexane; exhibits quaternary carbon atom; high octane number blending agent.

name: 2-Methylhexane
fact: Branched heptane isomer used in catalytic reforming to produce toluene.

name: 3-Ethylpentane
fact: Highly symmetrical triethylmethane isomer of heptane.

name: 2,4-Dimethylpentane
fact: Heptane isomer featuring two isopropyl groups linked by a methylene bridge.

name: Undecane
fact: 11-carbon paraffin used as sex pheromone by various ants and cockroaches.

name: Dodecane
fact: 12-carbon alkane component of diesel fuel and diluent in nuclear fuel reprocessing.

name: Tetradecane
fact: 14-carbon paraffin hydrocarbon used as phase change material for thermal energy storage.

name: Hexadecane
fact: Cetane; defines the 100-point standard for diesel fuel ignition quality (cetane rating).

name: Eicosane
fact: 20-carbon paraffin solid at room temperature; used in paraffin waxes and cosmetic bases.

name: 2,2,3,3-Tetramethylbutane
fact: Hexamethylethane; most highly branched and symmetrical octane isomer, melts at 100°C due to rigid crystal packing.

name: Squalane
fact: Fully saturated branched 30-carbon triterpane hydrocarbon; exceptionally stable cosmetic emollient.

name: Pristane
fact: 2,6,10,14-Tetramethylpentadecane; geochemical biomarker found in petroleum and shark liver oil.

name: 2-Methyloctane
fact: Branched nonane isomer found in petroleum and lavender volatile oil.

name: 3,3-Diethylpentane
fact: Tetraethylmethane; quaternary branched nonane isomer illustrating steric hindrance in free radical substitution.

name: cis-2-Butene
fact: Geometrical isomer of 2-butene with higher boiling point and net dipole moment due to cis configuration.

name: trans-2-Butene
fact: More thermodynamically stable geometrical isomer of 2-butene with zero net dipole moment.

name: 1-Pentene
fact: Terminal five-carbon alkene that yields 2-bromopentane via Markovnikov hydrobromination.

name: trans-2-Pentene
fact: Internal alkene formed as major Saytzeff product upon dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromopentane.

name: 2-Methyl-2-butene
fact: Amylene; tri-substituted alkene demonstrating superior thermodynamic stability over terminal isomers.

name: 1-Hexene
fact: Linear alpha-olefin co-monomer used industrially in linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) production.

name: Cyclohexene
fact: Six-membered cyclic alkene used in JEE to demonstrate anti-addition of bromine across double bonds.

name: 1,4-Pentadiene
fact: Non-conjugated diolefin containing an isolated methylene group between double bonds.

name: 1,5-Hexadiene
fact: Biallyl; classic substrate for [3,3]-sigmatropic Cope rearrangement at elevated temperatures.

name: Myrcene
fact: Acyclic monoterpene hydrocarbon with three conjugated/isolated double bonds; found in bay leaves and hops.

name: Ocimene
fact: Naturally occurring monoterpene triene isomer known for its sweet, herbal fragrance.

name: Allene
fact: Propadiene; simplest cumulene containing sp-hybridized central carbon with mutually perpendicular pi bonds.

name: 1,3-Pentadiene
fact: Piperylene; conjugated diene used in Diels-Alder cycloadditions with electron-deficient dienophiles.

name: 2,3-Dimethyl-2-butene
fact: Tetramethylethylene; fully substituted alkene possessing maximum hyperconjugation stability (12 alpha-hydrogens).

name: 1-Octene
fact: Important industrial alpha-olefin used as co-monomer in high-performance polyolefins.

name: 1,3-Cyclohexadiene
fact: Conjugated cyclic diene that readily undergoes [4+2] Diels-Alder cycloadditions in cisoid conformation.

name: 1,4-Cyclohexadiene
fact: Non-conjugated cyclic diene formed by Birch reduction of benzene with sodium in liquid ammonia.

name: Squalene
fact: Polyunsaturated all-trans triterpene hydrocarbon; key biosynthetic precursor to all plant and animal steroids.

name: Norbornene
fact: Bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-2-ene; strained bridged bicyclic alkene that undergoes ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP).

name: alpha-Pinene
fact: Bicyclic monoterpene alkene found in pine resin; contains a strained four-membered cyclobutane ring.

name: 2-Butyne
fact: Dimethylacetylene; internal symmetrical alkyne that undergoes Birch reduction to trans-2-butene.

name: 1-Pentyne
fact: Terminal alkyne that forms a red precipitate of cuprous acetylide with ammoniacal CuCl.

name: 2-Pentyne
fact: Unsymmetrical internal alkyne; hydration with HgSO4/H2SO4 gives a mixture of pentan-2-one and pentan-3-one.

name: 1-Hexyne
fact: Six-carbon terminal alkyne; reacts with sodamide (NaNH2) in liquid ammonia to form a nucleophilic sodium acetylide.

name: 2-Hexyne
fact: Internal alkyne isomer; undergoes Lindlar catalyst hydrogenation to stereospecifically yield cis-2-hexene.

name: 3-Hexyne
fact: Diethylacetylene; symmetrical internal alkyne producing solely hexan-3-one upon oxymercuration-hydration.

name: 1-Heptyne
fact: Seven-carbon terminal alkyne used in transition-metal catalyzed Sonogashira cross-coupling reactions.

name: 1-Octyne
fact: Standard terminal long-chain alkyne employed in click chemistry azido-alkyne cycloadditions.

name: Phenylacetylene
fact: Terminal aryl alkyne exhibiting acidic sp C-H bond (pKa ~28.8); trimerizes to 1,2,4- and 1,3,5-triphenylbenzene.

name: Tolan
fact: Diphenylacetylene; rigid rod-like diarylalkyne synthesized by double dehydrobromination of stilbene dibromide.

name: Vinylacetylene
fact: But-1-en-3-yne; formed by copper-catalyzed dimerization of acetylene; industrial precursor to chloroprene.

name: 2-Methyl-1-buten-3-yne
fact: Branched conjugated enyne intermediate in the industrial synthesis of synthetic rubber monomers.

name: 1,7-Octadiyne
fact: Terminal dialkyne capable of intramolecular cyclotrimerization to bicyclic aromatic rings.

name: 1,4-Pentadiyne
fact: Skipped diynes with active central methylene protons flanked by two electron-withdrawing triple bonds.

name: Ethynylcyclohexane
fact: Terminal alkyne bearing a bulky cyclohexyl substituent used in steric studies of hydroboration.

name: Cycloheptane
fact: Seven-membered cycloalkane; undergoes rapid pseudorotation among chair and twist-chair conformations.

name: Cyclooctane
fact: Medium-ring cycloalkane exhibiting significant transannular strain (Prelog strain) between opposing ring hydrogens.

name: Cyclononane
fact: Nine-membered ring cycloalkane with twist-chair-boat conformational equilibrium and moderate transannular crowding.

name: Cyclodecane
fact: Ten-membered ring with boat-chair-boat minimum energy conformation minimizing transannular H-H repulsions.

name: Methylcyclopentane
fact: Five-membered ring with single methyl substituent; isomerizes to cyclohexane over aluminum chloride catalyst.

name: Methylcyclohexane
fact: Demonstrates A-value steric energy; methyl group preferentially adopts equatorial position (95% at 25°C).

name: 1,1-Dimethylcyclohexane
fact: Gem-dimethylcycloalkane containing forced axial and equatorial methyl groups regardless of ring flip.

name: trans-1,2-Dimethylcyclohexane
fact: Chiral cycloalkane whose most stable diequatorial conformer possesses C2 symmetry without meso plane.

name: cis-1,2-Dimethylcyclohexane
fact: Meso compound in rapid ring-flip conformational equilibrium between two enantiomeric axial-equatorial forms.

name: trans-1,4-Dimethylcyclohexane
fact: Highly stable diequatorial chair conformer with center of inversion symmetry and zero dipole moment.

name: cis-1,3-Dimethylcyclohexane
fact: Diequatorial meso isomer favored by ~23 kJ/mol over diaxial conformer due to severe 1,3-diaxial strain.

name: trans-Decalin
fact: Rigid fused bicyclic alkane with trans-ring junction; incapable of chair-chair conformational inversion.

name: cis-Decalin
fact: Flexible fused bicyclic alkane with cis-ring junction that undergoes rapid conformational chair-chair flipping.

name: Norbornane
fact: Bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane; rigid bridged bicyclic alkane famous for non-classical carbocation studies in solvolysis.

name: Adamantane
fact: Diamondoid cage hydrocarbon with Td symmetry; completely strain-free repeating chair cyclohexane subunits.

name: Cubane
fact: Synthetic platonic hydrocarbon with 90° C-C-C bond angles; possesses immense strain energy (~695 kJ/mol).

name: Spiropentane
fact: Simplest spiro-hydrocarbon sharing a single quaternary spiro-carbon between two cyclopropane rings.

name: Bicyclo[2.2.2]octane
fact: Symmetrical bridged bicyclic hydrocarbon with eclipsed ethano bridges, illustrating torsional strain without angle strain.

name: Prismane
fact: Ladenburg benzene valence isomer with triangular prismatic carbon skeleton; extraordinarily strained polycyclic cage.

name: Quadricyclane
fact: Highly strained tetracyclic valence isomer of norbornadiene formed upon UV irradiation; candidate for solar thermal fuels.

name: 1-Chloropropane
fact: Primary alkyl chloride synthesized by treating propan-1-ol with thionyl chloride (SOCl2) in pyridine.

name: 2-Chloropropane
fact: Isopropyl chloride; undergoes SN1 solvolysis faster than 1-chloropropane due to secondary carbocation stability.

name: 1-Bromopropane
fact: Industrial solvent and cleaning agent prepared by free radical addition of HBr to propene in the presence of peroxides.

name: 2-Bromopropane
fact: Formed as Markovnikov addition product of HBr to propene without peroxides.

name: 1-Iodopropane
fact: Prepared by Finkelstein reaction of 1-chloropropane with sodium iodide in dry acetone.

name: 2-Iodopropane
fact: Readily undergoes E2 dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic KOH to regenerate propene.

name: 1-Chlorobutane
fact: Primary butyl chloride used to synthesize organolithium reagent n-butyllithium (n-BuLi).

name: 2-Chlorobutane
fact: Chiral secondary alkyl chloride illustrating Walden inversion during SN2 substitution.

name: 1-Bromo-2-methylpropane
fact: Isobutyl bromide; primary halide that undergoes rearrangement during SN1 solvolysis to form tert-butyl carbocation.

name: 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane
fact: tert-Butyl bromide; classic benchmark substrate for tertiary SN1 and E1 reaction mechanisms.

name: 1,2-Dichloroethane
fact: Ethylene dichloride; major industrial intermediate produced by chlorine addition to ethene for PVC manufacturing.

name: 1,1-Dichloroethane
fact: Ethylidene chloride; geminal dihalide that undergoes alkaline hydrolysis to yield acetaldehyde.

name: 1,2-Dibromoethane
fact: Vicinal dibromide formed by decolorizing reddish-brown bromine water with ethylene.

name: 1,1,2,2-Tetrachloroethane
fact: Acetylene tetrachloride (Westron); non-flammable solvent synthesized by catalytic addition of chlorine to acetylene.

name: Hexachloroethane
fact: Camphor-like subliming solid chlorocarbon used in military smoke grenades and pyrotechnics.

name: Chloral
fact: Trichloroacetaldehyde; reacts with chlorobenzene in conc. H2SO4 to yield the pesticide DDT.

name: Iodoform
fact: Triiodomethane; canary yellow crystalline precipitate formed in the iodoform test for methyl ketones and ethanols.

name: Bromoform
fact: Tribromomethane; heavy liquid (density 2.89 g/cm3) used as mineral separation heavy liquid and sedative precursor.

name: Trichloroethylene
fact: Industrial degreaser (Westrosol) synthesized by dehydrochlorination of 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane with Ca(OH)2.

name: Halothane
fact: 2-Bromo-2-chloro-1,1,1-trifluoroethane; milestone non-flammable general inhalational anesthetic containing four distinct halogens.

name: Pentan-1-ol
fact: 1-Pentanol; primary amyl alcohol used as solvent in pharmaceutical coatings.

name: Pentan-2-ol
fact: Secondary alcohol that yields pentan-2-one upon oxidation with acidified K2Cr2O7.

name: Pentan-3-ol
fact: Symmetrical secondary alcohol that gives negative iodoform test despite secondary hydroxyl.

name: 2-Methylbutan-1-ol
fact: Optically active component of industrial fermentation fusel oil.

name: 2-Methylbutan-2-ol
fact: tert-Amyl alcohol; tertiary alcohol with sedative properties, resistant to mild oxidants.

name: 3-Methylbutan-1-ol
fact: Isoamyl alcohol; chief component of fusel oil responsible for characteristic whiskey aroma.

name: Hexan-1-ol
fact: Fatty alcohol with fresh grassy fragrance; utilized in perfumery and plasticizer manufacturing.

name: Heptan-1-ol
fact: Linear 7-carbon alcohol used in cosmetics as fragrance fixative.

name: Octan-1-ol
fact: 1-Octanol; hydrophobic standard solvent used to determine 1-octanol/water partition coefficients (log P).

name: Propane-1,2-diol
fact: Propylene glycol; non-toxic antifreeze and pharmaceutical humectant synthesized by hydration of propylene oxide.

name: Propane-1,3-diol
fact: Trimethylene glycol; bio-derived monomer used with terephthalic acid to produce polytrimethylene terephthalate (PTT).

name: Butane-1,4-diol
fact: 1,4-Butanediol; industrial precursor to tetrahydrofuran (THF) and polybutylene terephthalate (PBT).

name: Butane-2,3-diol
fact: Vicinal diol existing in dextro, levo, and optically inactive meso diastereomeric forms.

name: Pinacol
fact: 2,3-Dimethylbutane-2,3-diol; undergoes classic acid-catalyzed pinacol-pinacolone carbocation rearrangement.

name: Pentaerythritol
fact: Neopentyl tetra-ol produced by multiple aldol condensations of formaldehyde with acetaldehyde; nitrated to PETN explosive.

name: Allyl Alcohol
fact: Prop-2-en-1-ol; allylic alcohol that selectively oxidizes to acrolein using active manganese dioxide (MnO2).

name: Propargyl Alcohol
fact: Prop-2-yn-1-ol; terminal alkyne alcohol synthesized by high-pressure ethynylation of formaldehyde.

name: Benzyl Alcohol
fact: Primary benzylic alcohol formed alongside benzoate salt via disproportionation in the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde.

name: 2-Phenylethanol
fact: Phenethyl alcohol; major aroma constituent of rose petals, synthesized by reacting phenylmagnesium bromide with oxirane.

name: Cinnamyl Alcohol
fact: 3-Phenylprop-2-en-1-ol; aromatic allylic alcohol with sweet floral balsamic odor occurring in storax and Peru balsam.

name: o-Cresol
fact: 2-Methylphenol; ortho-isomer extracted from coal tar; used as disinfectant and chemical intermediate.

name: m-Cresol
fact: 3-Methylphenol; meta-isomer precursor to thymol and various agrochemicals.

name: Resorcinol
fact: Benzene-1,3-diol; gives dark violet coloration with neutral FeCl3; component of resorcinol-formaldehyde adhesives.

name: Hydroquinone
fact: Benzene-1,4-diol; readily oxidized to p-benzoquinone; used as photographic reducing developer.

name: Pyrogallol
fact: Benzene-1,2,3-triol; alkaline solution rapidly and quantitatively absorbs atmospheric oxygen.

name: Phloroglucinol
fact: Benzene-1,3,5-triol; classic example of keto-enol tautomerism between aromatic triol and cyclohexanetrione.

name: 1-Naphthol
fact: alpha-Naphthol; used in Molisch's test for carbohydrates, developing a purple ring at the acid interface.

name: 2-Naphthol
fact: beta-Naphthol; couples with benzene diazonium chloride in basic medium to form brilliant orange-red dye Sudan I.

name: o-Nitrophenol
fact: Volatile with steam due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding (chelation), enabling separation from p-nitrophenol.

name: p-Nitrophenol
fact: Higher boiling point and non-steam-volatile due to strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

name: 2,4-Dinitrophenol
fact: 2,4-DNP; cellular metabolic poison that uncouples oxidative phosphorylation across mitochondrial membranes.

name: Picric Acid
fact: 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol; intensely acidic phenol (pKa 0.38) due to strong resonance stabilization by three nitro groups.

name: Thymol
fact: Natural monoterpenoid phenol found in thyme oil; antiseptic active ingredient in mouthwashes.

name: Carvacrol
fact: Isomer of thymol with pungent oregano odor; inhibits bacterial cell membrane integrity.

name: BHT
fact: Butylated hydroxytoluene; sterically hindered lipophilic phenolic antioxidant that scavenges free radicals.

name: Guaiacol
fact: 2-Methoxyphenol; naturally occurring aroma component formed by pyrolysis of wood lignin.

name: Eugenol
fact: Major aroma constituent of clove oil (~80%); used as dental analgesic and antiseptic.

name: Isoeugenol
fact: Formed by base-catalyzed isomerization of eugenol; industrial precursor to artificial vanillin.

name: 4-Aminophenol
fact: Synthesized by electrolytic reduction of nitrobenzene in acidic medium via phenylhydroxylamine rearrangement.

name: Salicyl Alcohol
fact: Saligenin; aglycone of salicin from willow bark, possessing mild analgesic and antipyretic activity.

name: Dipropyl Ether
fact: Symmetrical aliphatic ether prepared by bimolecular dehydration of propan-1-ol at 140°C with conc. H2SO4.

name: Diisopropyl Ether
fact: Volatile ether prone to rapid dangerous organic peroxide formation upon air exposure.

name: Dibutyl Ether
fact: High-boiling aliphatic ether solvent for Grignard reagents and organolithium reactions.

name: MTBE
fact: Methyl tert-butyl ether; octane-boosting gasoline additive synthesized by acid-catalyzed addition of methanol to isobutylene.

name: ETBE
fact: Ethyl tert-butyl ether; bio-based gasoline oxygenate prepared from bioethanol and isobutylene.

name: Phenetole
fact: Ethyl phenyl ether; synthesized via Williamson ether synthesis by reacting sodium phenoxide with ethyl bromide.

name: Diphenyl Ether
fact: Thermally robust diaryl ether used with biphenyl in eutectic Dowtherm A heat transfer fluids.

name: Dioxane
fact: 1,4-Dioxane; versatile aprotic cyclic diether miscible with water, prepared by dehydrating ethylene glycol.

name: Trioxane
fact: 1,3,5-Trioxane; cyclic trimer of formaldehyde used as fuel solid and precursor to polyoxymethylene engineering plastics.

name: 12-Crown-4
fact: Cyclic tetramer of ethylene oxide; crown ether tailored to selectively complex lithium cations (Li+).

name: 15-Crown-5
fact: Cyclic pentamer of ethylene oxide; crown ether with cavity size matched for selective sodium cation (Na+) encapsulation.

name: 18-Crown-6
fact: Nobel-prize winning crown ether that strongly complexes potassium cations (K+), solubilizing KMnO4 in benzene ('purple benzene').

name: Dimethoxymethane
fact: Methylal; simplest formal acetal synthesized by condensing formaldehyde with two equivalents of methanol.

name: 1,1-Diethoxyethane
fact: Diethyl acetal; stable to bases and nucleophiles, used as protecting group for the aldehyde carbonyl function.

name: Ethylene Oxide
fact: Oxirane; highly strained three-membered cyclic ether that undergoes ring opening with nucleophiles under mild conditions.

name: Propylene Oxide
fact: Methyloxirane; chiral epoxide produced industrially for polyether polyols used in polyurethane foams.

name: Tetrahydropyran
fact: Saturated six-membered cyclic ether (oxacyclohexane); ring framework of pyranose carbohydrate sugars.

name: Oxetane
fact: Four-membered strained cyclic ether that undergoes cationic ring-opening polymerization to polyethers.

name: Eucalyptol
fact: 1,8-Cineole; bicyclic monoterpenoid ether with fresh camphoraceous odor found abundantly in eucalyptus oil.

name: Diglyme
fact: Bis(2-methoxyethyl) ether; tridentate high-boiling coordinating diether solvent for hydroboration and reduction reactions.

name: Pentanal
fact: Valeraldehyde; 5-carbon straight-chain aliphatic aldehyde with pungent fruity odor.

name: Hexanal
fact: Fresh green-grass aroma aldehyde formed by oxidative degradation of linoleic acid.

name: Heptanal
fact: Oenanthaldehyde; produced industrially by pyrolytic vacuum distillation of castor oil.

name: Octanal
fact: Citrus aroma aldehyde occurring naturally in orange peel essential oils; used in perfumery.

name: Nonanal
fact: Pelargonic aldehyde; floral-rose scent component used in classic floral perfume accords.

name: Decanal
fact: Capraldehyde; important aroma chemical imparting sweet orange rind nuance.

name: Isobutyraldehyde
fact: 2-Methylpropanal; branched isomer formed during hydroformylation (oxo process) of propene.

name: Pivalaldehyde
fact: 2,2-Dimethylpropanal; lacks alpha-hydrogens, cleanly undergoing Cannizzaro disproportionation.

name: Acrolein
fact: Propenal; simplest alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde, formed by thermal dehydration of glycerol with KHSO4.

name: Crotonaldehyde
fact: But-2-enal; formed by self-aldol condensation of acetaldehyde followed by acid-catalyzed dehydration.

name: Cinnamaldehyde
fact: trans-3-Phenylpropenal; active essential oil giving cinnamon its characteristic warm flavor and scent.

name: Salicylaldehyde
fact: Prepared by Reimer-Tiemann reaction of phenol with chloroform in aqueous sodium hydroxide.

name: p-Nitrobenzaldehyde
fact: Strongly activated aromatic aldehyde used in Indigo synthesis via the Baeyer-Drewson reaction.

name: Anisaldehyde
fact: 4-Methoxybenzaldehyde; sweet hawthorn aroma, TLC stain reagent for terpenes and steroids.

name: Glyoxal
fact: Simplest dialdehyde; yellow liquid produced by catalytic vapor-phase oxidation of ethylene glycol.

name: Succinaldehyde
fact: Butanedial; versatile precursor used in Robinson's classic one-pot tropinone alkaloid synthesis.

name: Glutaraldehyde
fact: Pentanedial; potent dialdehyde chemical sterilant and protein cross-linking fixative for electron microscopy.

name: Terephthalaldehyde
fact: Symmetrical aromatic dialdehyde used as rigid cross-linker in covalent organic frameworks (COFs).

name: Furfural
fact: Heterocyclic aromatic aldehyde derived from agricultural pentosan biomass by acid hydrolysis.

name: Citral
fact: Geranial/neral mixture; unsaturated monoterpene aldehyde with strong lemon odor, found in lemongrass oil.

name: Pentan-2-one
fact: Methyl propyl ketone; positive iodoform test due to methyl ketone functionality.

name: Pentan-3-one
fact: Diethyl ketone; symmetrical dialkyl ketone that yields negative iodoform test.

name: Hexan-2-one
fact: Methyl butyl ketone; neurotoxic metabolite capable of inducing peripheral neuropathy via 2,5-hexanedione formation.

name: Hexan-3-one
fact: Ethyl propyl ketone; unsymmetrical ketone prepared by hydration of 3-hexyne.

name: 3-Methylbutan-2-one
fact: Methyl isopropyl ketone; branched methyl ketone with single acidic alpha-proton on one side and three on the other.

name: MIBK
fact: Methyl isobutyl ketone; 4-methylpentan-2-one; major industrial solvent synthesized by aldol condensation of acetone followed by selective hydrogenation.

name: Pinacolone
fact: 3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-one; classic product of acid-catalyzed pinacol rearrangement with tertiary-to-secondary methyl shift.

name: Di-tert-butyl Ketone
fact: 2,2,4,4-Tetramethylpentan-3-one; extremely sterically hindered ketone that resists nucleophilic attack by Grignard reagents.

name: Cyclopentanone
fact: Five-membered cyclic ketone produced by dry distillation (pyrolysis) of calcium adipate.

name: Cycloheptanone
fact: Suberone; seven-membered cyclic ketone prepared by barium-catalyzed pyrolysis of suberic acid.

name: Benzophenone
fact: Diphenyl ketone; non-enolizable ketone that forms deep blue ketyl radical anion when treated with sodium metal.

name: Propiophenone
fact: 1-Phenylpropan-1-one; prepared via Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with propionyl chloride in anhydrous AlCl3.

name: 1,4-Benzoquinone
fact: Yellow crystalline conjugated diketone; classic electron-deficient dienophile in Diels-Alder cycloadditions.

name: 1,2-Benzoquinone
fact: o-Quinone; red, highly reactive conjugated ortho-dione formed by oxidation of catechol.

name: 1,4-Naphthoquinone
fact: Bicyclic quinone forming the structural core of vitamins of the K family (phylloquinone, menadione).

name: Anthraquinone
fact: Tricyclic yellow quinone synthesized by Friedel-Crafts reaction of phthalic anhydride with benzene; precursor to alizarin dyes.

name: Acetylacetone
fact: Pentane-2,4-dione; beta-diketone showing strong keto-enol tautomerism (~80% enol) stabilized by intramolecular H-bonding.

name: Acetonylacetone
fact: Hexane-2,5-dione; 1,4-diketone precursor in the Paal-Knorr synthesis of furans, pyrroles, and thiophenes.

name: Camphor
fact: Bicyclic monoterpene ketone possessing a rigid bridgehead skeleton; sublimes readily at atmospheric temperature.

name: Carvone
fact: Chiral monoterpenoid ketone; (R)-isomer smells of spearmint while (S)-isomer smells of caraway seeds, illustrating chiral receptor specificity.

name: Pentanoic Acid
fact: Valeric acid; pungent liquid found in valerian root; synthesized by carboxylation of butyl Grignard reagent.

name: Hexanoic Acid
fact: Caproic acid; six-carbon fatty acid responsible for characteristic goat odor; used in ester flavoring agents.

name: Octanoic Acid
fact: Caprylic acid; medium-chain fatty acid antimicrobial agent used in dairy sanitizers.

name: Decanoic Acid
fact: Capric acid; saturated 10-carbon carboxylic acid used industrially in synthetic ester lubricants.

name: Pivalic Acid
fact: 2,2-Dimethylpropanoic acid; sterically hindered neopentyl carboxylic acid that resists esterification and nucleophilic attack.

name: Malonic Acid
fact: Propanedioic acid; classic dicarboxylic acid that undergoes facile thermal decarboxylation to acetic acid.

name: Succinic Acid
fact: Butanedioic acid; key intermediate in the citric acid (Krebs) cycle, dehydrates cleanly to cyclic succinic anhydride.

name: Glutaric Acid
fact: Pentanedioic acid; dehydrates upon heating to form stable six-membered cyclic glutaric anhydride.

name: Adipic Acid
fact: Hexanedioic acid; produced on multi-million ton scale by nitric acid oxidation of cyclohexanol/cyclohexanone for Nylon 6,6.

name: Pimelic Acid
fact: Heptanedioic acid; biosynthesized from lysine in plants; precursor in biotin metabolic pathways.

name: Suberic Acid
fact: Octanedioic acid; originally isolated from cork (suber) by nitric acid oxidation.

name: Sebacic Acid
fact: Decanedioic acid; prepared by alkaline cleavage of castor oil; monomer for Nylon 6,10 and dioctyl sebacate plasticizer.

name: Maleic Acid
fact: (Z)-Butenedioic acid; cis-isomer that easily forms maleic anhydride upon gentle heating due to proximal carboxyls.

name: Fumaric Acid
fact: (E)-Butenedioic acid; trans-isomer, non-toxic food acidulant, does not form an anhydride without high temperature isomerization.

name: Phthalic Acid
fact: Benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid; readily forms cyclic phthalic anhydride; starting material for phenolphthalein dye.

name: Isophthalic Acid
fact: Benzene-1,3-dicarboxylic acid; meta-isomer used in unsaturated polyester resins and aramid fibers (Nomex).

name: Terephthalic Acid
fact: Benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid; para-isomer produced by catalytic aerial oxidation of p-xylene; monomer for Dacron/PET polyester.

name: Salicylic Acid
fact: 2-Hydroxybenzoic acid; prepared by the Kolbe-Schmitt reaction of sodium phenoxide with CO2 under pressure; acetylated to aspirin.

name: Mandelic Acid
fact: 2-Hydroxy-2-phenylacetic acid; synthesized by acid hydrolysis of benzaldehyde cyanohydrin.

name: Tartaric Acid
fact: 2,3-Dihydroxysuccinic acid; Louis Pasteur's historical resolution of its sodium ammonium salt launched the science of stereochemistry.
